newsitem.title: USA: NY's Pataki urges state senate to approve casinos.
newsitem.headline: NY's Pataki urges state senate to approve casinos.

text.p: New York Gov. George Pataki, saying the state was losing enormous revenues to out-of-state casinos, urged the state Senate approve a measure to allow such resorts in New York in a vote Tuesday.

"My personal view is that we are losing literally billions of dollars to casinos outside our state, on our borders, and to Indian casinos inside the state," Pataki told reporters in Albany, though he added the lawmakers should vote their consciences.

"We're getting all the negative social consequences without any of the economic benefits," the Republican governor concluded. Popular casinos in Atlantic City, N.J., and Connecticut have boosted those states' tax revenues, partly by drawing New York State residents.
Senate Majority Leader Joseph Bruno, R-Troy, has said he does not know if the bill has enough votes to win approval, which will hinge on how many Democrats vote in its favor.
The measure, which would let one casino be built in Niagara Falls, Buffalo and either Warren or Saratoga Counties, was approved by a previous legislature, but must be enacted twice.
And voters, in a referendum, also must approve the bill, which in a bid to rescue the Catskills as a resort area, would allow an unlimited number of casinos to be built there.

A variety of groups, including religous and environmental outfits, as well as lobbyists representing out-of-state casinos that would become competitors, oppose the bill. The New York State AFL-CIO on Tuesday said it was urging lawmakers to approve the measure as it would create jobs.
